source_title: Science ISRO GSLV-F17 Launch: EOS-05 Satellite Successfully Placed In Orbit, Gaganyaan Mission Next
source_excerpt:
A GSLV rocket carrying ISRO’s EOS-05 Earth observation satellite successfully lifted off from Sriharikota in Andhra Pradesh in a pre-dawn mission on Friday. The rocket blasted off from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre at 2:55 am IST.
Shortly after liftoff, the EOS-05 satellite was successfully injected into its intended sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit, marking a successful mission for India’s space agency.
“I am very happy to announce that the GSLV-F17 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the advanced Earth observation satellite EOS-05, the Geo-Imaging Satellite, into the intended and required orbit,” ISRO Chief Dr V Narayanan said after the launch.
Thomas Kurian, Mission Director for the GSLV-F15 rocket mission, described the launch as a major milestone for the programme, saying EOS-05 was the heaviest satellite ever launched by the GSLV into a GTO or sub-GTO orbit.
“It is a moment of great pride and happiness for all of us. The success of GSLV has completed its 19th mission, and the mission carried the EOS-05, a uniquely configured Earth observation satellite capable of near-real-time imaging,” he said.
Kurian added that the satellite’s successful launch was the result of months and years of rigorous work, despite the launch itself lasting only a few minutes.

The mission carried EOS-05, an Earth observation satellite designed to provide India with a continuous bird’s-eye view from nearly 36,000 kilometres above Earth.
The GSLV-F17 launch vehicle stands 51.7 metres tall and has a liftoff mass of 420.5 tonnes, making it one of India’s largest operational launch vehicles.
Science and Technology Minister Jitendra Singh welcomed the successful mission and said India’s space capabilities were continuing to reach new heights, strengthening the country’s position as a global space power.
“EOS-05 is a state-of-the-art Earth Observation satellite and India’s first imaging satellite from geosynchronous orbit, enabling advanced imaging across visible, infrared, multispectral and hyperspectral bands,” Singh wrote on X.
The successful EOS-05 launch also came as ISRO continues preparations for the Gaganyaan programme.
ISRO chief Narayanan said “vigorous, systematic work” was underway for the launch of the first uncrewed Gaganyaan mission during the current calendar year. Speaking after the EOS-05 launch, he said preparations for the mission were progressing “very vigorously and systematically”.
Narayanan also praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his leadership and said ISRO has six more launches planned for the current financial year. The missions include the launch of the NVS-03 navigation satellite.
ISRO launched the EOS-05 Earth observation satellite on Friday at 2:55 am IST. It lifted off from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh.
The EOS-05 satellite is designed to provide India with a continuous bird's-eye view from approximately 36,000 kilometres. It is India's first imaging satellite from geosynchronous orbit, capable of advanced imaging.
EOS-05 is the heaviest satellite ever launched by the GSLV into a GTO or sub-GTO orbit. This mission also marked the GSLV's 19th successful mission.
ISRO is preparing for the first uncrewed Gaganyaan mission, targeted for this calendar year. Six more launches, including the NVS-03 navigation satellite, are also planned for the current financial year.

## मिशन का विवरण
भारतीय अंतरिक्ष अनुसंधान संगठन (ISRO) ने शुक्रवार को तड़के 2:55 बजे आंध्र प्रदेश के सतीश धवन अंतरिक्ष केंद्र से GSLV-F17 रॉकेट के माध्यम से EOS-05 अर्थ ऑब्जर्वेशन सैटेलाइट को सफलतापूर्वक लॉन्च किया। लॉन्च के तुरंत बाद, सैटेलाइट को उसके निर्धारित सब-जियोसिंक्रोनस ट्रांसफर ऑर्बिट में स्थापित कर दिया गया।

## तकनीकी विशेषताएं
* **क्षमता:** EOS-05 GSLV द्वारा GTO या सब-GTO कक्षा में प्रक्षेपित अब तक का सबसे भारी उपग्रह है।
* **इमेजिंग:** यह जियोसिंक्रोनस कक्षा से भारत का पहला इमेजिंग उपग्रह है, जो विजिबल, इंफ्रारेड, मल्टीस्पेक्ट्रल और हाइपरस्पेक्ट्रल बैंड में उन्नत इमेजिंग प्रदान करने में सक्षम है।
* **कवरेज:** यह उपग्रह लगभग 36,000 किलोमीटर की ऊंचाई से पृथ्वी का निरंतर दृश्य प्रदान करने के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया है।

## आगामी मिशन
19वें सफल GSLV मिशन के बाद, ISRO अब अपने आगामी लक्ष्यों पर ध्यान केंद्रित कर रहा है। ISRO प्रमुख डॉ. वी. नारायणन ने पुष्टि की है कि गगनयान के पहले मानवरहित मिशन के लिए काम व्यवस्थित रूप से चल रहा है, जिसे चालू कैलेंडर वर्ष में लॉन्च करने का लक्ष्य रखा गया है। इसके अलावा, चालू वित्तीय वर्ष के लिए छह और मिशनों की योजना है, जिसमें NVS-03 नेविगेशन सैटेलाइट का लॉन्च भी शामिल है।

आधिकारिक जानकारी की पुष्टि के लिए, कृपया ISRO की आधिकारिक वेबसाइट या उनके अधिकृत सोशल मीडिया चैनलों को देखें।

en_body:
## Mission Overview
India's space agency, ISRO, successfully launched the EOS-05 Earth observation satellite on Friday at 2:55 am IST. The mission utilized a GSLV-F17 rocket, which lifted off from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh. Following the liftoff, the satellite was successfully injected into its intended sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit.

## Technical Significance
* **Payload Capacity:** EOS-05 is the heaviest satellite to be launched by a GSLV vehicle into a GTO or sub-GTO orbit.
* **Imaging Capabilities:** As India's first imaging satellite from a geosynchronous orbit, it provides near-real-time data across visible, infrared, multispectral, and hyperspectral bands.
* **Operational Reach:** The satellite is designed to offer a continuous view of Earth from approximately 36,000 kilometres.

## Future Outlook
Following this successful 19th GSLV mission, ISRO is shifting its focus toward upcoming objectives. ISRO Chief Dr. V. Narayanan confirmed that preparations for the first uncrewed Gaganyaan mission are proceeding systematically, with a target for launch within the current calendar year. Additionally, the agency has planned six more missions for the current financial year, including the deployment of the NVS-03 navigation satellite.
